title: Write the thought down and pass it to a project
description: Fast entry and a few saved destinations: a work document, a project folder or a personal archive.

blocks.text: The phone is sometimes the place of capture while work on the text continues in another editor. Nobody needs an intermediate system of folders just to hand a short entry over.

quote.text: I have been a longtime user of Drafts, but I have tended to under-utilize it. It is designed around a concept that is appealing: simply start writing, then figure out what you want to do with it.

blocks.text: Open the input field first, then offer the saved actions: add to a chosen document or create a file in a project. Before the hand-off the destination is visible, after it the confirmed result.

The original stays until the hand-off succeeds. After a failure a retry should not create duplicates nobody notices. For the first destinations it matters more to keep the headings, links and attachments than to offer the user a scripting language.
